Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Rubya Haider and Sharmin Akhter walk in with their blades for Bangladesh Women. Rosemary Mair has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The Bangladeshi spinners once again stepped up. Their bowlers are making a habit of making things difficult for the opposition and New Zealand Women were their new victim. Marufa Akter had an off day but the spinners did their job perfectly. Rabeya Khan was the pick of the bowlers as she scalped three wickets. However, an overall effort sees Bangladesh Women end the innings with momentum on their back. There is no doubt Bangladesh Women have struggled with the bat in this tournament but one big innings and they could be in the game. The first 10 overs could be the key for both teams. Stay tuned as the chase is just around the corner.

Brooke Halliday is up for a quick chat. She says there wasn't much chat with Sophie Devine but they just tried to stretch the game. Mentions in India, the spinners usually love to bowl, so she tried to play sweeps and reverse sweeps. Reckons Bangladesh Women made it quite difficult as they have bowlers who bowl a lot of slower balls.

New Zealand Women won the toss and chose to bat first. Their top three, under pressure to get some runs in the tournament, failed today as well. (Suzie Bates, however, got off the mark in this tournament but an unfortunate run out cost her the wicket). New Zealand Women, in a bit of trouble at 38/3, were looking for answers and the skipper stepped up once again. She played the second fiddle to Brooke Halliday, who took the attack against the Bangladeshi bowlers. Their partnership got New Zealand Women back on track, but once both fell, New Zealand Women fell like a pack of cards.

New Zealand Women crawl their way to a respectable total. By no means was it an easy wicket to bat on and New Zealand Women were made to work hard for every run. For Bangladesh Women, their spinners once again stepped up, doing the bulk of the job and will be happy with the score they have put New Zealand Women to.
